title: The Impact of 3D Soft Tissue Simulation on Expectations and Satisfaction with Orthognathic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
Background: In people whose jaws are not correctly aligned, surgery can correct the position of the upper and/or lower jaw. This often also changes the appearance of the face. Most patients are satisfied with the result, but some are not – often because they had imagined something different beforehand. When the operation is planned on the computer, it is possible to calculate in advance how the face will probably look after surgery (three-dimensional facial simulation). Whether it helps to show patients this simulation before the operation has hardly been studied so far.
Research question: We want to find out whether showing this simulation during the pre-surgery information talk helps patients to better understand the operation, to have clearer expectations and to be more satisfied after the operation.
Methods: 30 adults who undergo jaw surgery at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery of Jena University Hospital can take part. Chance (drawing lots using sealed envelopes) decides whether they are shown the simulation during the information talk or receive the usual information talk without the simulation. All participants fill in a short questionnaire after the information talk and about six weeks and nine months after the operation. Six weeks after the operation, a three-dimensional image of the face is also taken to check how accurately the simulation predicted the actual result. The operation itself is carried out as usual, independently of the study.

interventions.name: Arm 1: Patients with dysgnathia receive a presentation of their individual photorealistic 3D soft-tissue simulation prior to a mono- or bignathic corrective osteotomy
Arm 2: Passive control group (without showing the individual photorealistic soft-tissue simulation)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients scheduled for single-jaw or bimaxillary orthognathic surgery who are treated at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery/Plastic Surgery, Jena University Hospital
- Ability to give informed consent to study participation
- Sufficient language comprehension (German or with the help of professional interpreting) to reliably understand and answer the study information, consent form and questionnaire
- Willingness to participate in the pre- and postoperative surveys according to the study protocol
Exclusion criteria:
- Age under 18 years
- Pre-existing facial malformations (e.g. syndromic conditions, cleft lip and palate)
- Limited capacity to consent or inability to give informed consent
- Insufficient language comprehension if reliable informed consent and completion of the questionnaire are not possible even with professional interpreting
- Previous orthognathic surgery (revision surgery)
